ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories at three levels: (i) by the Swiss notary during identity verification; (ii) by the fiduciary preparing the Art. 927a OR UBO filing; and (iii) by the accepting Swiss bank under AMLA Arts. 3-6 and the Swiss Banking Due Diligence Agreement. Required screening lists include the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Swiss SECO sanctions measures, and FINMA public notices. Foreign PEP status must be treated as high risk and domestic Swiss PEPs as medium risk, with enhanced due diligence including corporate ownership tracing to a natural person, source-of-funds documentation, negative-news review of trading counterparties, geographic risk rating of the scrap-copper supply chain, and document retention for at least 10 years under AMLA Art. 37.
ubo_and_aml_profiling._ubo_register_note: Beneficial ownership information filed under Art. 927a OR is collected by the cantonal commercial registry and made available to Swiss authorities only; it is neither published on Zefix nor accessible to the general public.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index of the Federal Commercial Registry Office (FEDRO), https://www.zefix.admin.ch
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to Arts. 951-954 OR, the firm must comply with the principles of truthfulness, clarity, and non-deception and must be written in Latin characters. The company name may be composed in German, French, Italian, or Romansh according to the official language of the canton of the registered office (German for the Canton of Zug). Freely invented or foreign-language terms (e.g., English) are admissible only where they are expressible in Latin script, contain no symbols, and do not mislead as to legal form, business purpose, or ownership. The legal-form suffix must appear as 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG'; transliterations such as 'stock corporation' are not accepted in the register. The name must be clearly distinguishable from all firms already registered in every Swiss canton, as verified through Zefix.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Sparkasse / Finanz (requires FINMA banking license or will be refused)
Versicherung / Assurance / Insurance (requires FINMA insurance license)
Trust / Trustee / Treuhand (triggers fiduciary licensing and AML scrutiny)
Schweizer / Swiss / Suisse / Helvetia (protected by the Swiss coat-of-arms law, SR 232.21; prior authorization required)
Eidgenössisch / Federal / Bundes- (misleading sovereign affiliation; generally refused)
Rotes Kreuz / Red Cross (protected emblem under the Geneva Conventions and SR 232.21)
Holding (permitted only where the company genuinely performs controlling holding functions)
Recycling / Recycled / Green (must be substantively true under UWG, SR 241.1, or will be refused as misleading)
Börse / Securities / Clearing (reserved for licensed financial market infrastructure operators)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the cantonal commercial registry rejects the proposed name or imposes a corrective condition, the founding notary first assesses whether the deed can be amended and resubmitted immediately. Where a formal refusal (Verfügung) is issued, the applicant may (1) request reconsideration in writing to the same registry within 30 days of service; (2) file an administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority for commercial registers (kantonale Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde) under Arts. 70-71 HRegV within the same 30-day window; (3) appeal further to the cantonal administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) and ultimately to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) on questions of law. Because Swiss incorporation timelines are tight, the recommended practice is to file a parallel new preliminary name inquiry and reserve an alternative name so that the commercial registration is not blocked while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted only in qualified form. The AG must have a physical registered office (Rechtssitz) in the canton of incorporation where Swiss authorities, creditors, and legal process can reach the company. A pure virtual mail-forwarding address without any local physical presence is rejected by the commercial registry and by Swiss banks. A written Sitzdomizil agreement with a licensed Swiss fiduciary is standard and acceptable for a cross-border scrap-trading vehicle, provided the fiduciary maintains the physical premises, handles official correspondence, and the books are accessible in Switzerland. Tax substance expectations for the trading entity include the ability to demonstrate administration, decision-making reachability, and documentation at the Swiss seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for ordinary registry-based inspections (estimated 3-5% probability of unannounced on-site verification, normally triggered by third-party complaint or evident abuse). A moderate probability of substantive physical or documentary review arises during Swiss federal and cantonal tax audits and during bank-conducted enhanced due diligence for the medium-risk scrap-copper line. SECO export-control and sanctions checks on cross-border non-ferrous scrap consignment may request warehouse, weighing, and transport evidence, but unannounced site visits remain the exception rather than the rule.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Arts. 620-659 (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Register Ordinance (VZV/ORC), Arts. 32-57; Swiss Act on Civil Law and Notarial Formalities, Art. 217.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce), Canton of Zug / Zurich / Geneva as selected by registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts), signed subscription declaration, and application for entry in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory share capital is CHF 100,000; at least 20% of each share's nominal value, and in any event a minimum of CHF 50,000, must be paid up and confirmed via escrow release from a Swiss bank before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: On the effective date, the sole founder of CH__CH__CH_AG__ISIC_4669_02_RECYCLED_SCRAP_COPPER_WIRE Aktiengesellschaft resolved as follows: 100,000 registered shares at CHF 1.00 par value are subscribed and fully paid up to the statutory minimum. The registered office is established at [Place, Canton, Address]. The following officers are appointed with individual/collective signatory authority: [CEO], [President], and [Corporate Secretary]. The officers are empowered to execute all Commercial Register filings, open banking accounts, engage notaries, and initiate the required waste-trading license application. The board also approves the procurement of premises, insurance coverage, and the adoption of corporate governance manuals. All resolutions are effective immediately and recorded in the official minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Confirmation and Drafting of Notarized Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office / Notary Public for the chosen canton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Swiss notary to verify the proposed company name is available and compliant with Swiss company naming rules. Draft the Articles of Association in the official local language, specifying corporate object, registered office, share capital, share classes, board composition, and audit requirements. Perform preliminary screening for reserved or misleading names via the electronic Commercial Register index (Zefix).
required_dossiers: Financial capacity statement for initial capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected, submit alternative name within 5 working days or appeal the decision before the cantonal supervisory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and Capital Escrow Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public and Swiss Chartered Bank of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain notarial authentication of the Articles of Association, incorporating the subscribed shares and capital structure. Open a temporary escrow account in the company name and deposit the required minimum paid-up capital. The bank issues a 'Bank Confirmation of Share Capital' (Bestätigung über die Einzahlung des Aktienkapitals) to be produced to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: List of board members with signatures
Criminal record certificate of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register rejects the capital confirmation, immediately rectify the bank form or obtain a revised written confirmation from the bank; re-submit with the same application package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File form 'C1 (Commercial Register Application)' together with the notarized statutes, capital confirmation, and board declarations. After approval, register the legal entity, obtain its Commercial Register identification (UID), and await publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a query, supply a notarized supplementary declaration or amend the Articles within 10 working days; if refused, file an appeal to the Cantonal Court within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Waste Management Authority and Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a waste-trade permit application pursuant to the Swiss Waste Ordinance (VVEA) for brokering and physical consignment of non-ferrous scrap copper wire. Provide corporate identity documents, storage facility description, procedures for waste transfer registration, and evidence of qualified waste manager or designated environmental officer. For cross-border movement, obtain the corresponding transboundary movement authorization under the Waste Movement Ordinance (OMoD).
required_dossiers: Description of physical consignment and storage operations
Facility plan indicating storage areas and containment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit application is incomplete, cure the deficiency within 30 days of notification. If the permit is denied, request reconsideration before the same authority and subsequently appeal to the cantonal administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authority of Representatives and Operational Governance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office; independent audit authority (statutory auditor); Swiss regulator for anti-money laundering (Conditionality MiBa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Update the Commercial Register with banking mandates and signatory powers. Execute the corporate seal policy, implement AML-compliant due diligence procedures for high-value scrap transactions, appoint an external audit firm if required, and adopt operational policies consistent with the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML risk tier.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register requires adjustments to signatory scope, execute a correcting resolution and re-file; administrative fines apply only after continued non-compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Waste Management Authority (Amt für Abfallwirtschaft) and Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Waste Trading Permit under the Swiss Waste Ordinance (VVEA), Art. 32; Transboundary Waste Movement Authorization under the Waste Movement Ordinance (OMoD)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) / Cantonal EIA Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening Classification: C – No mandatory full EIA report for pure physical consignment and scrap trading; a simplified registration and compliance declaration is required if covered storage or mechanical sorting is performed on-site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge controlled under the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV); diffuse emissions of dust and particulates must comply with federal Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) thresholds; storage areas must be impermeable, spill-containment equipment provided, and waste consignment documentation retained for a minimum of 10 years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by cantonal fire prevention authority confirming compliance with VKF/AEAI guidelines; structural load inspection certificate for racking and storage equipment; SUVA occupational safety and workplace health clearance confirming low-voltage electrical wiring and material handling risks are mitigated; emergency response plan approved by the relevant cantonal civil defense office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), portal: www.estv.admin.ch; direct corporate income tax is administered jointly by the ESTV and the cantonal tax authorities (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung, e.g., Steuerverwaltung Kanton Zug) and the municipal tax offices; VAT is exclusively administered by the ESTV Main Division Value Added Tax (Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer) through its e-VAT portal (eMWST). Customs export procedures are handled by the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS / Oberzolldirektion BAZG).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) obtains its statutory business identification number UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, format CHE-116.XXX.XXX) automatically upon entry in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister) at the relevant cantonal registry. For Swiss VAT, separate registration with the ESTV is required: registration is mandatory when the net turnover from taxable supplies in Switzerland exceeds CHF 100,000 within a calendar year (Art. 10 Swiss VAT Act); voluntary registration is available below this threshold (Art. 11 VAT Act). The UID simultaneously constitutes the VAT number (shown with the suffix 'MWST' / 'TVA'), superseding the former separate MWST-Nr. A foreign entity without Swiss Commercial Register entry must apply to the ESTV for a UID and VAT registration, submitting a written application (formular 030e), power of attorney, board resolution, certified certificate of incorporation and excerpt from the foreign commercial register, proof of Swiss business address or Swiss representative, and a declaration of turnover. Direct tax registration follows automatically with the competent cantonal tax authority after commercial registration; within 60 days the tax administration issues a file number and provides the annual corporate tax return package.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the AG is a body corporate subject to unlimited Swiss corporate income tax (CIT) on its worldwide income at cantonal, communal and federal level, with two statutory territorial carve-outs: (i) permanent establishments situated abroad and (ii) foreign immovable property are exempt in Switzerland but taken into account for the progression factor (Art. 52 Swiss Federal Direct Tax Act, DBG). Core rates: federal CIT 8.5% on post-tax profit (approximately 7.83% effective on a pre-tax basis); combined cantonal/communal rates vary between approximately 11.9% in Zug and 21.0% in Geneva/Zurich for ordinary income. No pass-through regime is available for an AG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for an AG. Available statutory elections and reliefs: (1) VAT group taxation election (Art. 13 VAT Act) for Swiss group entities, treating the group as one taxable person; (2) corporate income tax group taxation (Steuergruppe, Art. 61-67 DBG) enabling profit and loss pooling among Swiss group members; (3) participation exemption election (Art. 69-70 DBG) for qualifying dividends and capital gains on participations held at minimum 10% or with market value of at least CHF 1 million; (4) cantonal notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying equity capital; (5) tax ruling/advance tax ruling (Vorbescheid/Tax Ruling) with the competent cantonal tax authority and ESTV for certainty on transfer pricing, substance, and financing structures; (6) partial taxation of dividend income under Art. 18b DBG for substantial individual shareholders. Hybrid mismatch elections do not exist in Swiss federal law; abusive hybrid financing arrangements are subject to recharacterization under Swiss tax avoidance doctrine and the Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT; Mehrwertsteuer/TVA/IVA) levied under the Swiss VAT Act of 12 June 2009 (Bundesgesetz über die Mehrwertsteuer, MWSTG), as amended; customs duties on imports are governed by the Customs Tariff Act and the Customs Act administered by the FOCBS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual net turnover derived from taxable supplies in Switzerland (excluding VAT and exempt supplies; Art. 10 VAT Act). For a foreign company, the threshold is measured from Swiss-sourced taxable supplies with a place of supply in Switzerland; once CHF 100,000 is exceeded in a calendar year, compulsory registration applies with effect from the following year. Below the threshold, voluntary registration is possible, conferring the right to claim input VAT deduction. For the ISIC 4669 'cross-border physical consignment of non-ferrous scrap' business, physical export consignments are outside the scope/zero-rated; only the Swiss portion of turnover (e.g., domestic handling, commissions, storage in Switzerland) counts against the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory government-controlled e-invoicing platform, no digital stamping and no SAF-T filing mandate (as of 2025). Electronic and PDF invoices are fully valid if they satisfy the substantive legal requirements of Art. 26 VAT Act (name and address of the supplier and recipient, itemized description, quantity, date of supply, consideration, applicable rate). Common Swiss e-invoicing formats accepted for VAT purposes include Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung), SIX eBill, ZUGFeRD/Factur-X and XML-based formats; paper invoices remain permissible. Tax-relevant records, including invoices, customs declarations, and export evidence, must be archived in a tamper-proof manner for 10 years (Art. 81 VAT Act and Art. 958f Swiss Code of Obligations).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods qualifies for the 0% zero rate under Art. 23 VAT Act when: (i) the goods are physically transported from Swiss customs territory to a foreign country by the supplier, the buyer, or a third party acting for either; (ii) the supply is made for consideration and the recipient obtains the power to dispose of the goods; (iii) the export is established in a credible manner by the exporter holding the prescribed documentary evidence. For the subject business of shredded non-ferrous scrap copper wire (HS 7404), the Swiss AG must evidence that the goods have irrevocably left Swiss customs territory; transit through the EU must be documented as a transit procedure (NCTS/ATLAS). Transport to Liechtenstein is subject to special rules (not automatically zero-ratable). Because the output is taxed at 0%, the exporter retains the right to deduct input VAT on purchases and obtains periodic refunds from the ESTV insofar as input VAT exceeds output VAT; this is the primary VAT recovery mechanism for the exporter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (e-dec / NCTS export declaration) and validated exit certificate issued by FOCBS evidencing the goods' departure from Swiss customs territory

Commercial invoice (Rechnung) stating the exporter's UID/MWST-identification number, commodity description 'shredded non-ferrous scrap copper wire', weight in tonnes, HS tariff code 7404, price and the express reference to zero-rating under Art. 23 VAT Act
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill or CMR/CIM transport document proving physical exit from Switzerland and the foreign destination
Contract or sales confirmation (order/purchase agreement) with the foreign counterparty defining delivery terms (Incoterms) and transfer of title/risk
Customs import declaration or other destination-country customs evidence (e.g., EU summary declaration ATLAS) corroborating arrival in the foreign customs territory
Bank or payment documents: SWIFT/TT confirmation, documentary letter of credit and compliant negotiation documents, or inward remittance certificate, evidencing receipt of the foreign consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV and the FOCBS conduct risk-based audits on export dealers in scrap metals (high-risk sector: precious and non-ferrous metals). If the export documentation is found to be false, incomplete or inconsistent, the zero-rating is retrospectively overturned and the unconditional tax is claimed at the standard rate (8.1%) plus arrears interest published periodically by the ESTV (approximately 4.5% per annum in the current notification cycle). Input VAT deductions are disallowed retroactively. Under the Swiss VAT Act, tax evasion (Art. 197) is punishable by a fine up to three times the tax evaded; intentional diminution of VAT revenue (Art. 196) carries a fine of CHF 1,000 to CHF 200,000 (or to CHF 800,000 under aggravating circumstances); negligent conduct attracts fines and administrative penalties. Presenting forged or false documents to customs constitutes evasion of customs duties under Art. 96 ff. of the Customs Act (ZG), with imprisonment up to two years or substantial fines. Violations may also expose directors to criminal liability under Swiss criminal law. Statute of limitation for recovery of VAT is generally five years, and up to ten years in case of evasion; clawback claims for incorrectly credited export refunds follow the same limitation periods. In addition, false export documentation triggers reputational risk with financing banks under Swiss anti-money laundering obligations (GwG), as scrap metal trading is considered a medium-risk sector requiring enhanced documentary verification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) in coordination with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking conduct and anti-money laundering supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current- and capital-account convertibility under the Swiss Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments and the Federal Act on the Free Movement of Capital. The Swiss franc (CHF) is freely floating with no surrender, approval, or restriction on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or repatriation of invested capital. No distinction is drawn between resident and non-resident accounts for conversion purposes. Foreign exchange transactions are not rationed and no prior authorization is required for cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts. Swiss law imposes no obligation to convert foreign currency proceeds into CHF, nor a timeline for repatriation of export earnings. Companies may retain funds in any freely convertible currency and settle invoicing in any agreed currency, provided the transaction is documented under Swiss commercial and banking regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. Swiss law does not provide for European-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing under FINMA. Entities from EEA/UK cannot passport an EMI authorization into Switzerland. Foreign digital EMIs may only provide payment services to Swiss clients through a supervised Swiss banking or FinTech licensee (Art. 1b Banking Act). For cross-border physical metals trading, a traditional Swiss bank account or a fully licensed Swiss FinTech institution is required; unlicensed offshore EMIs are not a viable alternative for holding corporate funds or conducting SWIFT transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted under Swiss anti-money laundering (AMLA) regulations using video identification provided the process is performed by a FINMA-compliant provider or a licensed Swiss financial intermediary. However, for a medium-risk enhanced commodity trader in recycled scrap metal, most tier-1 banks impose a mandatory in-person or video interview with at least one director or the authorized signatory, and may require a local Swiss resident representative (e.g., a licensed fiduciary or lawyer) for compliance monitoring. Physical presence is not legally prescribed, but practically expected for non-resident directorship structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual ownership structure with non-resident shareholders or nominee arrangements for a Swiss AG engaged in commodity trading.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the Articles of Association, Commercial Register extract, ultimate beneficial ownership declarations, complete shareholding registry, notarized deeds of formation, and a formal explanation of the commercial rationale for the ownership structure. Provision of audited financial statements or bank reference letters from prior financial institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trading counterparties or goods originating from jurisdictions subject to sanctions or enhanced monitoring, such as certain Eurasian or Middle Eastern trade corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed supply chain documentation including origin certificates, bills of lading, supplier due diligence files, sanctions screening results, and an end-to-end goods flow description (from purchase of scrap copper wire to final delivery). A written risk assessment in line with AMLA Art. 8 and any relevant FINMA circular 2023/06 guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction velocity and currency mismatches (CHF, USD, EUR) typical of recycled metal cross-border clearing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro forma commercial invoices, sale contracts, LC drafts, and a 12-month cash-flow forecast demonstrating that all payments are backed by signed trade documentation. Provision of internal AML/KYC policies, employee training records, and a designated compliance officer mandate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loans to the Swiss AG must be wired via SWIFT MT103 with clear remittance information. Recommended purpose codes: 'KAPITALEINLAGE' (capital contribution) or 'DARLEHEN' (shareholder loan) for capital injections; for ordinary trade advances, 'HANDELSGESCHAEFT' (trade transaction). The receiving Swiss bank will require the remitter to be identified on the company's approved payer list and will verify the economic substance of the transaction against the Commercial Register and the company's charter. No exchange control declaration is necessary. For capital increases, the funds must be credited to a blocked escrow account (not the operating account) prior to the notarial confirmation of the capital increase registration with the Commercial Register.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for physical shipment of shredded copper scrap should be routed through SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) or SWIFT MT202 (bank-to-bank) for payment against documents. For larger buy-sell operations, a Commercial Letter of Credit (confirmed or unconfirmed) is recommended, with the Swiss bank issuing an MT700 series; negotiation can be done on a sight or usance basis. For transactions within the European Economic Area, the bank may use the SEPA Direct Credit scheme only for euro-denominated payments with a valid creditor IBAN, but for non-EU counterparties, SWIFT is the mandatory clearing rail. All outbound payments should reference the underlying contract number and invoice ID to support bank-side monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign exchange forwards (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF) with a Swiss banking counterparty under master agreements
FX swaps on major convertible currencies (EUR/USD/CHF/GBP) in accordance with ISDA/DFSAs
Call and put currency options on freely convertible currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps where all currencies are fully convertible and not subject to exchange controls

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for currencies with no onshore deliverability; Swiss banks may execute NDFs as an offshore derivative but they are not a standard instrument for CHF or EUR pairs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, management report, and federal/cantonal corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (for cantonal and federal direct tax) with Swiss Federal Tax Administration as coordinating body
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For financial year ending 31 December, filing due by 30 June of the following year; extensions generally available upon written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty, default assessment, and late-payment interest at approximately 5% p.a.; repeated or willful non-compliance triggers fines under cantonal tax law and Swiss Direct Federal Tax Law (DBG), and enforced collection measures ('Betreibung') may eventually lead to forced dissolution; no automatic strike-off for tax arrear.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory audit report (ordinary or limited audit) presented to the shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General shareholders' meeting; audit report also kept for inspection by the commercial register office, tax authorities, and creditors on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The shareholders' meeting must be held within six months after balance sheet date (Art. 699 CO); the audit report must be available to shareholders before that meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors' personal liability for failure to comply; court may order a shareholders' meeting at the company's cost; if an audit is required and omitted, the commercial register office may withhold subsequent filings and a penal complaint may be filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register data confirmation and event-driven registration updates (registered office, directors, share capital, status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual calendar deadline for event-driven changes; updates must be filed without undue delay, typically within 30 days of the triggering event; certain cantonal offices may require an annual confirmation of registered details for domiciliation companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Noncompliance with commercial register obligations is subject to administrative fines (up to CHF 10,000) imposed by the commercial register supervisory authority; repeated failure to comply may trigger an official deletion procedure after formal notice and appeal period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual share register and beneficial-owner register review and update (if bearer shares or applicable UBO regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; no filing to a Swiss authority, but records must be available for inspection by FINMA, cantonal tax authorities, and public prosecutors upon lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The registers must be continuously current; an annual review is recommended at the shareholders' meeting, and share transfers must be recorded as they occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Knowingly making false or incomplete entries in the UBO register is punishable under Art. 697p CO by a fine of up to CHF 10,000; failure to maintain the share register can lead to director civil liability; no automatic administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Art. 727 CO, an ordinary audit is required for a Swiss AG exceeding two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total of CHF 20,000,000, turnover of CHF 40,000,000, and 250 full-time employees on annual average. All other companies require a limited audit (Art. 727a CO); a small company may voluntarily opt out of the limited audit only through a unanimous shareholder resolution (Art. 727a para. 2 CO).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) accounting rules equivalent to Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS is permitted for statutory accounts of listed companies and for consolidated financial statements; taxable income is based on statutory accounts with prescribed tax adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no statutory annual filing of a beneficial-owner register with a Swiss authority. The AG must maintain a register of beneficial owners only if bearer shares are issued or if otherwise required under Art. 697i CO. For registered shares, the company records ownership in the share register. All share transfers must be reported without delay; annual confirmation is internal only and must be available for official inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register for registered shares)
Register of Share Transfers (record of transfers)
Register of Beneficial Owners (when bearer shares are issued)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 3,500 per year for Swiss domiciliation and registered office services in non-premium cantons; USD 3,500 - 6,500 for enhanced corporate service provider packages
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Limited audit: USD 3,300 - 8,800; ordinary audit of a trading company: USD 11,000 - 22,000; increased to USD 25,000 - 40,000 if group consolidation or complex cross-border transactions are present

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal direct corporate income tax of 8.5% assessed on net profit after tax (effective 7.83% on pre-tax profit). The Canton of Zug imposes a combined cantonal/communal profit tax of approximately 11.9% on pre-tax profit for the ordinary trading company; the aggregate Swiss federal-plus-cantonal-plus-communal statutory burden for a Zug Aktiengesellschaft is thereforeapproximately 14.5% for tax year 2024.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation deduction (Art. 69/70 DBG): exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains from participations of at least 10% or with acquisition cost above CHF 1 million. Licence/Patent Box: up to 90% cantonal and 92.5% federal exemption of qualifying IP-derived income (Art. 24b DBG), available in Zug if substantive IP development occurs onshore. Research and development super-deduction of up to 150% for Swiss domestic R&D personnel costs. Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on qualifying excess equity at the Zug cantonal level. Capital tax base reduction: Zug applies a 50% reduction of taxable equity for cantonal/communal capital tax purposes. No specific manufacturing or export incentive applies to the recycled scrap copper wire trading activity; normal Swiss tax rates govern the AG.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal/cantonal annual tax return for corporations: 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen – Aktiengesellschaft' (Form 640 / cantonal Zug corporate return set). Filing is made annually through the Zug cantonal tax administration electronic portal (Canton Zug e-filing platform, supported by ESTV-certified software such as TaxMe/e-Zug) and, for federal direct tax, through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) e-filing infrastructure. The return is a single multi-sheet document covering federal, cantonal, and communal profit tax and capital tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed within six months after the close of the fiscal year. For a company with a 31 December balance-sheet date, the filing deadline is 30 June of the following calendar year. The Zug tax authority routinely grants an extension until 31 January of the second following year upon a written reasoned request; unauthorized late filing does not suspend the accrual of default interest and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit per the statutory Swiss financial statements (Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 958ff), adjusted for book-to-tax differences. This line must reconcile to the signed annual accounts of the AG.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG is taxed on its worldwide income; foreign-source income from the procurement and sale of recycled copper wire is included, with a foreign tax credit only where a relevant double-tax treaty application is documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-depreciation and value adjustments on movable fixed assets (maximum declining balance 40% per annum), intangibles, and provisions for diminution in value of the scrap inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Depreciation must follow the Swiss cantonal harmonized schedules; a non-resident parent group applying IFRS/US-GAAP depreciation cannot deduct higher foreign book rates for Swiss tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisions deductible under Art. 63 DBG: pending litigation, product/warranty liabilities, environmental remediation, and specific discernible risks of the scrap commodity trade. Future-cost provisions are disallowed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each provision must be individually substantiated with contemporaneous documents; over-accruals linked to related-party payables are treated as hidden profit distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses available for a maximum carryforward of seven years (Art. 67 DBG). No loss carryback is allowed under Swiss federal law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards survive a transfer of shares if economic identity is maintained; utilisation is denied in abusive transactions in which the scrap-trading activity is acquired solely for the tax-loss shell.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for the participation exemption (Art. 69/70 DBG) on dividends and capital gains from qualifying subsidiaries held directly or through qualifying intermediaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The lower-tier participation must carry real economic activity in its country of residence; treaty-shopping arrangements and artificial conduit structures forfeit the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable equity for cantonal/communal capital tax: paid-in share capital, capital reserves, retained earnings, and hidden reserves net of the 2020 reduction; Zug applies a 50% reduction to the computed equity base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG must file a schedule of shareholders and equity movements; distributions in kind of copper inventory to a foreign shareholder reduce equity and may trigger capital-tax recharacterisation if not at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable profit line after add-backs and deductions: accounting profit minus tax-exempt items (participation income, patent box) plus non-deductible expenses (Art. 59-63 DBG) such as excessive management fees, financial penalties, and unwarranted value adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible expenses include foreign taxes for which no credit is allowed and payments to a non-resident shareholder exceeding the arm's length standard; the non-resident must accept the AG's statutory-basis-only return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Election for the patent/IP licence box regime: 90% exemption in Zug of qualifying royalty income generated by Swiss-developed patents and comparable IP rights; federal exemption of 92.5% is coordinated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The scrap-copper trading company generally has no qualifying IP; electing the box without an internally developed patent triggers abuse penalties and retroactive reassessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign withholding taxes on foreign dividends, interest, royalties, and branch profits (Art. 69 Para 3 DBG), capped at the Swiss tax attributable to the foreign grossed-up income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Documentation must include foreign tax assessments, proof of beneficial ownership, and treaty certificates; without them the foreign tax is only a deductible expense at the AG level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Anti-Abuse Declaration and WHT Refund Guarantee
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of all foreign controlling shareholders, certification that dividends and distributions will be subject to the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax, and guarantee to disclose future distributions to the ESTV.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent applying for treaty refund of withholding tax must complete the official refund form (e.g., Form 823/823-HF), submit an annual residence certificate (TRC), and declare beneficial ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing sanctions: procedural fine 'Ordnungsbusse' up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 174 DBG); discretionary estimated assessment by the tax authority with an upward surcharge of 30-50% when the return is missing or incomplete; default interest of 3.5-4.5% per annum on any overdue tax; separate penalty of up to 50% of the reassessment for materially incorrect returns. Criminal prosecution for deliberate concealment of cross-border scrap sales (Art. 175/186 DBG) attracts fines up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to three years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax ('Verrechnungssteuer') on all distributions of profit by the AG, including cash dividends, constructive dividends, partial liquidations, and benefits-in-kind. The tax must be withheld from the gross distribution and remitted to the ESTV within 30 days of the value date; non-remittance creates a strict personal liability of the payment agent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder invokes the applicable double taxation agreement (DTA) by filing a refund application with the ESTV after the 35% tax has been remitted. Protocol for the standard foreign corporate shareholder: (i) obtain the AG's distribution statement and the official withholding tax certificate; (ii) obtain a certificate of residence (TRC) for the complete calendar year from the shareholder's tax authority; (iii) complete the official refund form (e.g., Form 823/823-HF) together with a declaration of beneficial ownership and title to the shares; (iv) submit the package through the ESTV refund process. As an example, under the Switzerland-China DTA the rate is reduced to 5% for shareholdings of at least 10% and to 10% for other dividends, subject to the anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership safeguards; different DTAs provide 0% or 5% rates. Refund claims are time-barred three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound royalties and interest are not subject to Swiss federal withholding tax when paid to non-residents on arm's length loan and licence arrangements; the 35% Swiss WHT is generally limited to dividends, interest on Swiss-issued bonds or bank deposits, and lottery winnings. Consequently, the AG may pay technical management, processing, and licence fees to a foreign parent free of Swiss source tax, provided the beneficiary is the economic owner and the amount is arm's length. Swiss-source interest on bonds issued by the AG to foreign investors and fiduciary instruments remains exposed to the statutory 35% rate when the loan is evidenced by a Swiss taxable bond. Foreign withholding taxes on royalties or interest received by the AG may be credited under Art. 69 DBG.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The ESTV transfer-pricing documentation guidance requires a Local File where annual cross-border related-party turnover reaches CHF 8,000,000 or more, or where intra-group financing balances exceed CHF 8,000,000. A Swiss Master File is expected for groups with consolidated revenue exceeding CHF 50,000,000 or when the foreign parent jurisdiction requires one. Below these thresholds, the Zug tax authority expects an arm's length statement and adequate contemporaneous evidence on the intercompany scrap procurement, processing, and sales margins.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no separate Economic Substance Regulations statute as found in certain offshore jurisdictions. However, economic substance is a core Swiss tax principle: the AG must demonstrate actual management and control in Switzerland, physical office premises, qualified staff, genuine decision-making, and real business risk absorption. A letterbox company is denied treaty benefits, withholding-tax refunds, and cantonal capital-tax reduction, and may be requalified as transparent for tax purposes. The OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test and the Swiss Federal Supreme Court jurisprudence on 'Scheingeschäfte' apply. The recycled scrap copper wire trading AG must therefore keep substance metrics: HR payroll, minutes of Swiss board meetings, warehouse/QC procedures, and transactional risk management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Federal and Cantonal Direct Tax)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a tax return that conceals or under-declares sales of shredded copper wire, recording fictitious purchases, using hidden foreign bank accounts, or booking personal expenses of the Swiss director as business costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessed tax plus default interest at 3.5-4.5%; administrative fine up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG); qualified tax fraud 'Steuerbetrug' (Art. 186 DBG) carries imprisonment up to three years; withdrawal of the commercial licence for repeated non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign an incomplete return are jointly and severally liable under Art. 754 Swiss Code of Obligations for resulting tax damage. Criminal conviction triggers restitution of evaded tax, confiscation of assets, travel restrictions and freezing orders (Art. 177 SchKG), disqualification from board office, and custodial sentences in severe fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the AG without Swiss business substance: no office, no local management, accounting and contracts entirely handled abroad, dividend pass-through to a foreign principal, and the Swiss entity merely holding the scrap trade invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax recharacterisation of the AG as tax-transparent with profit allocated to the foreign shareholder; denial of the 35% withholding-tax refund; 35% withholding on deemed constructive dividends; extra federal and cantonal tax plus 30-50% reassessment penalties; possible deregistration under Art. 913h CO.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto and nominal directors cannot invoke the corporate veil: they are personally liable for unpaid taxes, social security contributions, and VAT under Art. 52/53 DBG and SchKG 52; travel bans and the obligation to open the company books are imposed in insolvency proceedings; criminal sanctions for aiding a sham entity under Art. 146 CP apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Cash Transaction Non-Compliance (Scrap Commodity Sector)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Settling copper scrap purchases in cash or informal value-transfer systems, refusal to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of suppliers or buyers, issuing false invoices in a missing-trader (carousel) fraud, and failure to file STRs with the Swiss MROS when suspicious transactions arise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) exposes the trader to fines up to CHF 500,000 (Art. 14 GwG); money laundering under Art. 305bis CP carries imprisonment of one to five years; the entire cargo and trading proceeds are subject to confiscation under Art. 70 CP; VAT fraud under Art. 146 CP imposes separate custodial penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors approving unregistered cash settlements or omitting the UBO identification face criminal prosecution and personal confiscation; the AG's charter and insurance do not indemnify criminal fines; responsible officers may be banned from entering the EU/Schengen area while criminal proceedings are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring a dividend to a foreign parent without withholding and remitting the 35% federal tax, paying interest on a Swiss bond without deduction, repurchasing own shares disguised as capital repayment, or awarding benefits-in-kind to a shareholder free of tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The debtor company is required to pay the unwithheld tax itself plus interest of 3.5-4.5%; fines up to three times the tax amount under Art. 70 VStG; the AG may be liquidated by the ESTV if the tax remains unpaid after seizure of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as paying agents are personally liable for the 35% remittance irrespective of corporate fault; in bankruptcy, the responsible officer receives a travel ban and the obligation to reconcile the tax ledgers under SchKG 170; repeated deliberate omission triggers criminal tax prosecution for evasion of the withholding tax (Art. 65 VStG) with imprisonment up to two years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking a fixed or inflated intercompany margin to a related procurement entity in a low-tax jurisdiction without performance of actual functions, transfer of risk, or capital allocation; failing to prepare Local File and Master File when related-party turnover crosses the CHF 8 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Full income adjustment with 3.5-4.5% interest; penalty of up to 50% of the reassessed tax under Art. 175 DBG; reclassification of the excessive payment as a constructive dividend triggering 35% WHT and refund denial; treaty relief under MAP is only available with compliant documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing officers who knowingly approve non-arm's length transfer prices are criminally liable for qualified tax fraud (Art. 186 DBG) and civilly liable under Art. 754 CO for the shortfall; in insolvency, the Swiss tax administration pursues directors and de facto officers for restitution; foreign travel may be prohibited while the criminal investigation is active.
